# Polymux

Polymux's current source is a native SwiftUI app backed by a Go agent server. Native targets require macOS 27 or iOS 27. Conversations and agent execution belong to the connected server; the app keeps a local cache and presents the interface.

## Version scope

These facts describe current native source, whose Xcode project version is 0.4.0. They do not establish that a signed package is available for every target. The website's desktop download selection still follows the earlier Electron release line for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Inspect release assets and notes before installing.

Historical Electron releases and dated comparison articles describe a different interface. The current native app has no tabbed Hub, Drive, Browser, Tasks, or Subagents workspace. It has no general Providers, Models, Memory, Skills, or MCP settings page. Do not turn historical feature descriptions into native setup instructions.

## Native app

- A sidebar lists conversations, with name/role search, unread and active filters, and sorting.
- New Chat creates individual or group conversations with up to 16 agents.
- An agent's profile edits its name, role, role description, and avatar. Group headers edit the group's name and members.
- Conversations support file attachments, message replies, search, activity, and approval cards.
- Settings includes appearance, the agent-server address, voice, and notifications.
- Voice settings offer Cascaded and Full Duplex modes with Gemini configuration. Voice models are separate from the server's text model.

## Server and authentication

The Go server runs agents and stores authoritative history. Native text-model startup configuration uses model.json in the server data directory or POLYMUX_MODEL_URL and POLYMUX_MODEL. Credentials use supported environment injection or an absolute owner-only key file. The durable runtime uses an OpenAI-compatible provider. Saving a provider-registry entry is not equivalent to selecting the active runtime model.

Backend requests require device Bearer authentication. Local macOS discovery can use the default server's owner-only local credential. A server URL alone is not remote authentication. Do not expose an unauthenticated agent service or the host-controller interface to the internet.

## Agent capabilities

- Memory tools save, recall, and forget notes in SQLite, scoped to an agent and conversation. Memory resides on the server. Forgetting active memory does not erase chat history or backups.
- One-shot and interval routines run on the server. The native profile lists routines and offers cancellation and a background-review toggle. There is no general cron editor.
- spawn_task queues a bounded child task. Children receive explicit tasks, not the entire parent conversation or its private memory, and cannot recursively delegate.
- Trusted Markdown skills and stdio or Streamable HTTP MCP connections are configured per agent on the server. manage_integrations changes are made from direct user conversations and take effect on the next turn. The older ~/.polymux/mcp.json watcher instructions do not apply.

## Data boundaries

Messages and attachments are sent to the connected server. If it runs on another computer, data is not confined to the app device. Hosted model providers and configured tools can receive task content under their own terms. Server filesystem access is not automatic access to the app device's filesystem.

Microphone, speech, and notifications have separate purposes and permission requirements. Tool installation is not blanket authorisation to send, publish, pay, delete, or act on every connected account. Review approval requests and the integration's own controls.
